correctness.rationale: Re-audited corrected RESULT.md. The two conditional moment masses evolve by P^T diag(A,B); the positive initial mass has positive projection on a nonnegative left Perron eigenvector, so even zero multipliers do not invalidate necessity. The second eigenvalue is nonpositive, so sign det(I-M) measures strict stability. The factor h is positive; all terms of G(-t) are nonnegative with strictly positive constant, excluding any nonpositive root. The first discriminant then gives respectively three positive roots or one, and at zero its real root factorization gives a puncture for d<s or a collapsed upper window for s<d; a triple root leaves one interval. The original 'separated' phrasing was ambiguous because two open components need not enclose an interval of positive length. The repair states both notions and gives a concrete puncture with z=(1-q)h=5/4 double, 3/2 simple, q=(97+5 sqrt(745))/512, lambda=-(1+q)/(5/16+3q). The nested discriminant has negative sign below q_* and a single simple real lambda-zero, so positive endpoint values exclude all interior zeros. At q_* nonnegativity allows only the one interior even-multiplicity lambda-zero, where G has a triple root. Above q_* up to 1/2, simple lambda-roots cannot cross the endpoints (whose values stay positive); the rational alternating signs at q=49/100 certify an interior negative P and pin the two roots throughout. q=1/2 has an explicit negative evaluation, and for q>1/2 continuity from lambda=-1 gives an interior negative value. This proves necessity and sufficiency for existence including the case where the gap can be just a point. Exact bounded replay: python3 /workspace/repairs/2/check_boundary.py passed the nested discriminant, endpoint identities, cusp and puncture factorizations, earlier-slice determinant identity and all four rational witness checks (149481/200000, -147/6250, 83961/200000, -3501/3125). No packaged script was executed.

value.rationale: Re-audited the narrowed result: the all-contrast threshold tells which centered quadratic pairs can ever exhibit strict stable-unstable-stable steps under the allowed chains, rather than merely re-demonstrating that some pair can. In particular it detects a range below the deterministic-alternation contrast threshold, and separates an isolated marginal failure from loss over a positive-length range at the boundary. The exact algebraic frontier is a useful check for stability theory and parameter scans; numerical witnesses and the second-moment kernel are supporting evidence rather than the value claim.
